title: Free LLM - for building, agents, images, etc. (title from repo catalog .prism/shared/pot/catalog_local.json; no description file present)
core_takeaway: A guest (Tash/Tosh) demos an open-source project called Free LLM API: a local router that aggregates the free-tier quotas of ~45 model providers behind one unified API key, with automatic failover between providers serving the same model and a Thompson-sampling router that ranks models on reliability, speed and intelligence. He reports burning ~2.8 billion tokens (~$500 of value) at zero cost, and hands the unified key to coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Cline) via a copy-paste CLI setup command. The stated boundary: providers encourage this for prototyping and experimentation, but using free quotas in production apps is discouraged.
key_points: The dashboard shows ~2.8 billion tokens consumed and ~1.8 billion of monthly quota remaining, all from free tiers across providers.
Multiple providers often serve the same model, so they are bundled and an automatic fallback chain switches provider without changing the model — no silent mid-project model swap.
Distribution is broad: GitHub repo plus a macOS app, a Windows app, a Docker one-liner, a Google Play app and an iOS App Store app; the desktop app lives in the system tray.
Roughly 45 providers are configured; a dead provider key can be edited and replaced in the UI and traffic resumes.
The output is one unified API key you paste into an agent; an agents page carries automatic setup commands for Claude Code, OpenCode and Cline-style CLIs.
The router uses Thompson sampling (explore/exploit) to keep sending traffic to the best-ranked models while occasionally probing others to update the ranking.
Coverage is not text-only: embeddings for RAG, image, video and audio models, plus an experimental 'fusion' mode that combines multiple models into one output.
Providers reportedly encourage it — Alibaba is said to have asked for its models to be added as a funnel from free trial to paid usage.
Explicit caveat: some providers discourage free quotas in production codebases, so the guest recommends it for personal prototyping only.
why_it_matters: This is the routing layer a multi-agent suite eventually needs anyway — provider abstraction, health-aware failover, and a bandit policy that scores models on the axis you care about — implemented against free tiers rather than paid ones. The design worth stealing is not the free tokens but the shape: one key, per-model multi-provider bundles, and explore/exploit ranking so the router learns which backend is actually good for a given job. The production caveat means treat it as a prototyping fixture, not a runtime dependency.
